Cyber Attack Disrupts Curacao’s Ports and Payment Systems, Impacts BB Energy Holdings NV

WILLEMSTAD, June 14 – A major cyber attack targeting Curacao’s port logistics and electronic payment systems has brought economic activity on the Dutch Caribbean island to a standstill on Friday, affecting shipping operations, retailers, and fuel suppliers including BB Energy Holdings NV.

The attack, detected early Friday morning, crippled software handling container tracking and customs clearance at the Port of Willemstad, Curacao’s main cargo gateway. Simultaneously, point-of-sale terminals and online banking services across the island have experienced widespread outages, causing long lines at supermarkets and gas stations.

Port officials said all inbound and outbound cargo movements have been suspended until further notice due to the inability to process customs documentation electronically. “Our priority is to mitigate the impact on essential goods, but there is currently no way to clear shipments,” said Port Authority spokesperson Jeanette Maduro. More than 20 container vessels are reportedly anchored offshore, unable to dock or unload.

The Curacao Bankers Association confirmed that electronic payments, including card transactions and online transfers, are “intermittently unavailable” at most financial institutions. Some ATMs have also stopped functioning, prompting concerns about access to cash for residents and businesses.

BB Energy Holdings NV, a major supplier of fuel and lubricants to the island, reported disruptions to its shipping and distribution operations. “Our supply chain has been significantly affected by the port closure and payment system failures,” said a company representative. “We are working closely with authorities to restore operations and minimize the impact on customers.”

Authorities have not disclosed the origin or nature of the cyber attack, but an emergency committee including law enforcement and cybersecurity experts has been convened. “We are treating this as a serious threat to national infrastructure,” said Minister of Economic Development Javier Soliana. “Restoring critical services is our highest priority.”

The Curacao Chamber of Commerce warned the attack could have severe consequences if prolonged. “With both port and payment systems compromised, businesses are unable to receive goods or process transactions,” said Chamber President Lucia Martis. “This situation underscores our vulnerability and the urgent need for stronger cyber defenses.”

Union leaders expressed concern for workers affected by suspended operations across shipping, retail, and logistics sectors. “Many employees are worried about lost wages if this crisis continues,” said Fernando Diaz, head of the Dockworkers Union.

As of late Friday afternoon, officials said there was no clear timeline for resolution. Residents were urged to conserve cash and avoid unnecessary travel while the situation develops.
